newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa money mkt shortage above 11 billion rand.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa money mkt shortage above 11 billion rand.

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage stood at 11.117 billion rand on Saturday after rising to a record high of 11.126 billion rand on Friday, the Reserve Bank said on Monday.
Dealers said the rise in the shortage appeared to be linked to foreign exchange flows.

The shortage had been expected to rise during December, with some players predicting a shortage of 12 billion rand, primarily because of the rise in notes and coins in circulation as the Christmas spending period gathered pace.
Notes and coins were quoted at 23.263 billion rand on Saturday, unchanged from Friday.
The money market had already been under pressure because of the rand's renewed gyrations earlier in the month.
Andre Kock, general manager of the Reserve Bank's money and capital market division, said the rise in the shortage had been expected because of the "strange" flow of notes in December.
"This is within estimates and the market should probably settle within the next week or two. One must expect these sort of movements in the short term," Kock said.
